title: Show each Read/Search call instead of folding them into one summary line
description:
Consecutive Read, Search and List calls are folded into one summary line on the main screen. This keeps them out of the fold, so each shows as an ordinary tool row with its result. Thinking still folds into its own 'Thought for Xs' line between them.

The fold is a grouping pass over the message list, and it carries more than tool calls: thinking blocks are absorbed into the same group, and the group's summary line is the only place the main screen shows them — a raw thinking block renders nothing outside Ctrl+O or verbose mode. The earlier version of this patch dismantled the groups wholesale, which made every tool call visible and every thought invisible, and also lost PreToolUse hook summaries absorbed mid-group. Leaving the grouping alone and only declining to classify read/search/list as foldable avoids both: each such call becomes a break point, and the thinking around it groups exactly as before.

sites.description: The tool classifier deciding what may join a fold: takes (name, input, tools), handles memory, workshop and scratchpad writes, MCP calls and silently absorbed tools, and ends by asking the tool's own isSearchOrReadCommand.
The local combining the tool's own answer — isSearch || isRead || isList. Captured by what it is built from, so the edit below targets that name rather than trusting a minified letter.

`isCollapsible: <readSearch> || (fullscreen ? <bashLike> : false)`. Only the read/search/list operand is dropped. Fullscreen's bash folding, and the MCP, memory-write and other categories returned earlier in the classifier, keep upstream behaviour.

verify.describe: read/search/list no longer classified as foldable
